text: Debugging is an essential skill for any programmer, but it can be frustrating when code doesn’t work as expected. The first step is to identify the bug clearly—read the error message carefully and reproduce the problem to understand what’s going wrong. Instead of guessing, use a systematic approach: break the code into smaller parts and test each one. Debugging tools, such as breakpoints and step-by-step execution, help you inspect variables and find the exact line causing trouble. Additionally, adding logging to your code can track the flow of data and reveal hidden issues. With patience and methodical testing, most bugs become manageable.
